hints: Evaluate the given integral by parts with $u=\ln x$ and $dv=x^{1/2}dx$.
Complete the remaining power integral and apply the limits $1$ and $a$ before setting the result equal to $2$.
Collect the $a^{3/2}$ terms and rearrange without using decimal approximations to reach the displayed fixed-point relation.
walkthrough:
Apply integration by parts to $\int x^{1/2}\ln x\,\mathrm{d}x$ with $u = \ln x$ and $v' = x^{1/2}$:
$$u' = \dfrac{1}{x}, \quad v = \dfrac{2}{3}x^{3/2}$$

Formulate the integration by parts expression:
$$\int x^{1/2}\ln x\,\mathrm{d}x = \dfrac{2}{3}x^{3/2}\ln x - \int \dfrac{2}{3}x^{3/2} \cdot \dfrac{1}{x}\,\mathrm{d}x = \dfrac{2}{3}x^{3/2}\ln x - \dfrac{2}{3}\int x^{1/2}\,\mathrm{d}x$$

Evaluate the remaining integral:
$$\int x^{1/2}\ln x\,\mathrm{d}x = \dfrac{2}{3}x^{3/2}\ln x - \dfrac{2}{3}\left(\dfrac{2}{3}x^{3/2}\right) = \dfrac{2}{3}x^{3/2}\ln x - \dfrac{4}{9}x^{3/2}$$

Substitute the limits $x = 1$ and $x = a$ and equate to $2$:
$$\left[\dfrac{2}{3}x^{3/2}\ln x - \dfrac{4}{9}x^{3/2}\right]_1^a = 2$$
$$\left(\dfrac{2}{3}a^{3/2}\ln a - \dfrac{4}{9}a^{3/2}\right) - \left(\dfrac{2}{3}(1)^{3/2}\ln 1 - \dfrac{4}{9}(1)^{3/2}\right) = 2$$
$$\dfrac{2}{3}a^{3/2}\ln a - \dfrac{4}{9}a^{3/2} - \left(0 - \dfrac{4}{9}\right) = 2$$
$$\dfrac{2}{3}a^{3/2}\ln a - \dfrac{4}{9}a^{3/2} + \dfrac{4}{9} = 2$$

Multiply the entire equation by $9$ to clear denominators:
$$6a^{3/2}\ln a - 4a^{3/2} + 4 = 18$$
$$6a^{3/2}\ln a = 4a^{3/2} + 14$$

Divide by $3\ln a$ to isolate $a^{3/2}$:
$$a^{3/2} = \dfrac{7 + 2a^{3/2}}{3\ln a}$$

ai_rubric.Integration by Parts: Integrates by parts and reaches $ax^{3/2}\ln x+b\int x^{3/2}\frac1x\,dx$. Substitutes limits and equates to $2$. The final result is $a^{3/2}=\frac{7+2a^{3/2}}{3\ln a}$.

hints: Put part (i)'s relation in zero form, for example $F(x)=3x^{3/2}\ln x-2x^{3/2}-7$.
Evaluate $F(2)$ and $F(4)$ and use their opposite signs and continuity to bracket $a$.
walkthrough:
Rearrange the equation from part (i) into the form $F(x) = 0$:
$$F(x) = 3x^{3/2}\ln x - 2x^{3/2} - 7$$

Conclude using the intermediate value theorem:
Because $F(x)$ is continuous on $[2, 4]$ and changes sign between $x = 2$ and $x = 4$ ($F(2) < 0$ and $F(4) > 0$), there exists a root $a$ of $F(x) = 0$ in the open interval $(2, 4)$, proving that $a$ lies between $2$ and $4$.

ai_rubric.Numerical Root Bracketing: Endpoint evaluations at 2 and 4 establish the sign change or ordering. Endpoint evaluation gives $F(x)=3x^{3/2}\ln x-2x^{3/2}-7$, $F(2)\approx-6.78$ and $F(4)\approx10.3$, so $2<a<4$.

Verify the root to 3 decimal places using a sign-change test on the interval $[3.0305, 3.0315]$ with $F(x) = 3x^{3/2}\ln x - 2x^{3/2} - 7$:
- $F(3.0305) \approx -0.00360 < 0$
- $F(3.0315) \approx +0.00509 > 0$
Conclude that $a = 3.031$ correct to 3 decimal places.

ai_rubric.Fixed-Point Iteration: Substitution into $a_{n+1}=\left(\frac{7+2a_n^{3/2}}{3\ln a_n}\right)^{2/3}$ gives consecutive iterates $3.031\to3.0305\to3.0315$, converging to $a=3.031$.
